title: Accounts 101
productJob: A compact high-trust reference for deciding what must be known before pasting real material into an AI product; not a privacy notice, provider plan table or class.
audience: A reader with real work or personal material who needs a safe next action before using an AI product.
learnerOutcome: The reader can identify the exact tool/account, the material and her authority, find the governing policy and stop when any answer is unknown.

steps.name: Name the exact door
steps.purpose: Identify the product, account, workspace and any connected app or third-party action actually receiving the material.

steps.name: Name the material
steps.purpose: Identify whether it contains credentials, personal data, confidential work, client information, regulated data or contract-restricted content.

steps.name: Check your authority
steps.purpose: Confirm that the applicable employer, client, contract and data-classification rules permit this exact use in this exact account.

steps.name: Check the current provider rule
steps.purpose: Use the provider's current official privacy, data-use, retention, sharing and connected-service documentation for the exact product/account.

steps.name: Stop when unknown
steps.purpose: Do not paste the real material until the authorized owner resolves any missing answer; minimize, anonymize or use an approved route only when that is genuinely permitted.

decisionRule.nonRemedy: Later deletion may be available, but it does not turn an unauthorized disclosure into an authorized one and must not be the safety plan.
decisionRule.limitation: This reference is not legal advice and cannot authorize a tool, account, upload or data use.

temptingWrongAnswers.statement: It is paid, so I can paste the client deck.
temptingWrongAnswers.reason: Payment does not prove organizational approval, permitted data, contractual scope or provider behavior.

temptingWrongAnswers.statement: I used my work email, so it is approved.
temptingWrongAnswers.reason: An email address or work device does not by itself identify the governing contract, workspace or policy.

temptingWrongAnswers.statement: I will delete the chat afterward.
temptingWrongAnswers.reason: Deletion is not advance permission and cannot be assumed to reverse disclosure, processing or connected-service transfer.

temptingWrongAnswers.statement: The consumer training setting is off, so the NDA is irrelevant.
temptingWrongAnswers.reason: A provider setting cannot override a contract, client restriction, employer policy or lack of authority.

analogy.name: Elle reads the rule
analogy.mapping: Elle Woods wins by noticing the exact rule everyone else skipped; the useful move here is checking the governing account and policy before acting.
analogy.limit: The film scene is a memory cue, not privacy, security or legal evidence. The real answer comes from current official terms and the authorized owner.

ownership.privacyTerms: The LAiDIES Privacy and Terms pages own what this site itself collects, uses, retains and shares.
ownership.residentCard: Resident Card owns LAiDIES identity and continuation; it does not approve an external AI account.
ownership.toolCards: Maintained provider tool cards own current plan names, menu paths, settings and product-specific data behavior.
ownership.classes: SUNNYVAiLE High may own guided workplace scenarios and feedback; this book remains the pre-paste lookup rule.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.scope: Cross-sector risk-management source supporting governed, context-specific treatment of privacy, information security and organizational AI use.
sources.limitation: It does not decide an individual's contract, employer policy or provider account settings.

sources.title: Data Usage for Consumer Services FAQ
sources.scope: Current official example showing that data use depends on service, account and settings and that consumer and business offerings have different governing documentation.
sources.limitation: OpenAI-specific and subject to product, plan, region, setting and policy change.

sources.title: How do you use personal data in model training?
sources.scope: Current official example distinguishing consumer and commercial data roles and directing commercial users to customer policies and terms.
sources.limitation: Anthropic-specific and subject to product, plan, customer agreement and policy change.

freshness.owner: Library editorial, privacy and AI product accuracy owners
triggers: a cited provider materially changes data-use or account documentation
the LAiDIES Privacy, Terms or Resident Card boundary changes
a reader interprets payment, work email, a setting or deletion as authorization

correctionRoute.subject: Accounts 101 correction
correctionRoute.privacyBoundary: Name the section and a current public source; do not email passwords, account details, private files, personal data or confidential work material.

authorityBoundary: This source record is not legal advice, does not authorize an account or upload, does not alter LAiDIES Privacy/Terms, and does not admit or publish the book.
